purpose: Audit whether value scores change across empty reward exits and whether the artifact changes card ranking. Diagnose a public-state equivalence mechanism using existing data, without reopening ES or expanding samples.
scope: All 6264 E171 card menus, including all 1536 initial families. Contract only a recorded nonterminal parent REWARD_SKIP whose next state is MAP and whose full admitted public observation differs solely in the REWARDS/MAP one-hot columns. Targets must match. Preserve every other successor and report exclusions.
scoring: Use the same three family-excluding frozen E170 models, mask, independent NumPy computation and 1e-6 parent tie margin. No parameter, checkpoint, threshold or scope selection by outcome. Compare raw and canonical scores and outcomes; retain all families.
native: First four source initial menus, all recorded alternatives, no selection by outcome. Reproduce acquisition and contracted exit using recorded legal native actions with state/RNG checks; require no unclaimed reward choices. No fresh MCTS game.
limits: This diagnosis uses recorded public successors; no live action adapter exists.
Empty exits can expose optional potion operations. The contraction is fixed-parent outcome-equivalent, not a claim that every legal policy must exit.
E169/E170 and E171 retain their failed original gates. No automatic adoption or additional sampling follows any diagnostic result.
These are historically exposed families, not final unused acceptance.
